_comment: Job boards are CONFIGURATION, not code. The token is the slug in boards.greenhouse.io/<token> and in the API path /v1/boards/<token>/jobs. Going from one company to fifty is an edit to this file and nothing else -- no code change, no test change. Nothing here is derived from any user's profile; this source is shared exactly like the LinkedIn pool.
_shape_comment: A board is { source, token, domain?, name? } plus its source's own fields (workday: host, tenant, site, facets; comeet: company_uid, api_token -- both public, embedded in the company's own careers page; lever: name is required). source is the job system (greenhouse, workday, lever, comeet), token its id there, and source:token the board key every stored posting, queue message and run-ledger row is identified by. An unknown source, a key listed twice or one domain on two boards is fatal at load. This file was companies.json until 2026-09-28 (docs/plans/board-config.md); the old shape still loads.
_boards_comment: Each token here is justified by MEASURED London engineering supply, because the failure mode is silent: a board with London jobs but no engineering ones scores a London engineer against account executives and looks like it is working. similarweb has 6 London jobs and NOT ONE is engineering (4 sales, 2 data science). monzo carries 49 London jobs, 16 engineering -- but every one is backend, Android, analytics or management, so a front-end or full-stack candidate still matched nothing: measured end to end, Maya (TypeScript/React/Node) drew four Monzo backend roles and a product designer, top score 44, all NO. deliveroo is here to close that: 129 jobs, 63 London, 27 London engineering, including Senior/II/Staff Software Engineer - Full-Stack. Measured 2026-09-22 -- boards change, so re-check rather than trust this line. The ten after deliveroo were chosen 2026-09-26 from the companies in the retired LinkedIn pool that have a Greenhouse board, each board's company_name checked against the pool's (a first-word token can be a different company: 'iai' is i.AI, 'axon' is the US Axon), ranked by engineering roles located in Israel or the UK, remote excluded: nebius 36 IL + 43 UK, wayve 5 + 57, catonetworks 27 + 4, nice 10 + 17, via 10 + 2, scaleops 10, payoneer 10, connecteam 10, taboola 10, transmitsecurity 10 (keyword counts from the boards API -- the ingest's pre-read filter and its check lines are the real measure). Added in a batch of ten so each batch's filter lines can be read before the next. Batch 2 (2026-09-26), same method, the rest of the pool's boards with real Israel/UK engineering supply: jfrog 7 IL + 2 UK, fireblocks 7 + 2, zscaler 3 + 6 (380 postings, most elsewhere -- the pre-read filter skips them), worldquant 4 + 5, melio 7, eleoshealth 7, axonius 6, forter 5, unframe 5 (its domain is unframe.ai; unframe.com is another company), appsflyer 4. What the pool has left after these is boards with 0-4 such roles, or a different company behind the token. Batch 3 (2026-09-26): three Greenhouse boards the name-guessing missed because the token is not the name -- found by looking up each company's careers page: wizinc (Wiz, 13 IL + 3 UK), gongio (Gong, 10 IL), nextinsurance66 (Next Insurance, now ERGO NEXT, 8 IL).
_workday_comment: Workday boards (docs/plans/workday-adapter.md) name the company's own careers site: host/tenant/site from https://<host>.myworkdayjobs.com/<site>, and name because a Workday posting carries a legal entity. KLA's 'Israel' site is Israel-only, so it needs no facets (75 postings, 2026-09-28). A whole-company site needs facets to narrow it below Workday's 2000 cap, or it is never proven complete and nothing on it is closed: NVIDIA's are locationHierarchy1 = Israel (2fcb99c4...326c) and United Kingdom (2fcb99c4...32d2), 467 postings, listed whole on 2026-09-28. The facet key differs by tenant: CrowdStrike, F5, Motorola Solutions, Medtronic and Thales narrow by locationCountry = Israel (0845...d89a) and United Kingdom (2924...0bc7); Cisco has no country facet, so it lists its 11 Israel and UK cities under locations -- a city added later is missed until listed here. All six listed whole on 2026-09-28 (CrowdStrike 60, F5 16, Cisco 73, Motorola Solutions 86, Medtronic 52, Thales 115). Batch 2 (2026-09-29): Applied Materials by Country = the same Israel and UK ids (63; its whole site is at the cap); Intel by locations = Israel, Haifa / Israel, Kiryat-Gat / Israel, Petah-Tikva / Virtual United Kingdom (22) -- its whole site (605) is under the cap and could be listed whole, but that means ~145 'N Locations' detail reads a day; chosen narrow, so a new Intel site in Israel is missed until its id is added here.
_domains_comment: Each board's domain is its company's own web domain, for its logo -- the boards API returns none -- and for the one-domain-one-board rule. The token is a Greenhouse slug, not a domain, so it is written down rather than derived. Optional: a board with no domain gets its initial on the card. The ingest resolves logo_url_template per domain and stamps the URL on every row of that board, so the API never reads this file. Swapping the service -- e.g. to logo.dev, https://img.logo.dev/{domain}?token=pk_... -- is an edit to the template; the next run restamps every row.
_limits_comment: Embedding batch packing, and ONLY that. The model and its dimensions are deliberately NOT here: this file ships inside the ingestion image and the API cannot read it, so a model named here could differ from the one retrieval uses, and that failure is silent. They live in Greenhouse:Embedding (GreenhouseEmbeddingOptions), which both halves bind.
_budget_comment: The token budget is what a batch is FILLED to; max_batch_items caps how many texts go in one request regardless of size. voyage-4's real ceiling is 320K tokens -- over three times this -- so split-and-retry should never fire in production. It is implemented and tested anyway, because the 120K-limit families (voyage-4-large, voyage-3-large, voyage-code-3) are one config edit away, and then this number is the only thing between a run and a hard 400.
_served_locations_comment: The BASELINE of where the product's users are -- every profile's own location is added on top from pool_locations (learned on profile save), so a user in a new city needs no edit here. For the pre-read filter (Greenhouse__Prefilter=log|on): a NEW posting whose board location and offices name none of these is not read, embedded or stored. Whole words, case-insensitive, against the board's own free text -- so list cities as well as countries: a posting that says only 'Herzliya' is otherwise ruled out. 'Remote' reads every remote posting, including US-only ones; kept because a wrong skip is silent and an extra read is not. Empty list = no location filtering.
